title: ArcCivs 0.1.92 navigation and decorative-work repair: restored resident production sensitivity
assumptions: .92 changes navigation/discovery availability and removes zero-value Auto mining/planting scenery from the inventory journal; the existing 3 confirmed zero-progress forestry attempts and miner 330s next selection define the affected blocked-next-cycle scenario; earlier successful .91 receipts are excluded. Before is 0 affected future completions; the hypothetical restored scenario uses 6/24/72 completions as in the old assessment. This is not a whole-city zero.

This compares only the affected next-cycle baseline while the resident is stalled with a hypothetical restored navigation scenario. Before is zero affected completions; it does not claim the whole prior city earned nothing. The .90 forester had already completed one native-tree receipt and credited +3 abstract WOOD before stalling; that historical receipt is outside this forward-looking baseline.
Participants are 1/4/6 villages and active production time is assumed at 0.25/1/4 hours per village-day. These sensitivities are not telemetry, quotas or guaranteed throughput.

Restored L1 FORESTER scenario: 6/24/72 completed, replanted native trees per village-day. Each completed tree keeps the existing 4 abstract WOOD completion credit and 1 abstract WOOD seed-plot cost, for 3 net abstract WOOD per completed tree. This is the same configured per-completion amount and planting cost as before; navigation changes the chance of completing the next existing cycle, not its rate.

Restored L1 QUARRY scenario: 6/24/72 economic deliveries per village-day at 3 abstract STONE each. Credit requires the existing 60,000 ms observed-work session at ordinary hunger, successful travel to the real depot and the original durable delivery. Hunger at or below 6 doubles observed-work duration to 120,000 ms. Ore alternatives replace STONE cycles and are not additive.

Configured gross completion amounts remain FORESTER 4/8/12 abstract WOOD and QUARRY 3/6/9 abstract STONE at L1/L2/L3. The scenario uses L1 only. No rate, amount, seed cost, quota, cap, building price, item rule or economic/final-tree receipt changes. Only input/output-free visual subactions use ordinary gameplay persistence instead of an inventory journal; existing visual-only legacy journals retire without item/stock/XP credit.

Each completed economic/tree cycle grants 1 resident profession XP. The two independent L1 worker streams are FORESTER and QUARRY: after restoration they contribute 12/48/144 resident XP per village-day in aggregate; while stalled, affected next-cycle completions and XP are zero. No route, travel, native visual subaction or partial receipt grants additional XP.

Abstract WOOD, abstract STONE and resident profession XP are separate units. Native planting/replanting remains governed by the existing paid seed-plot rule and final-tree receipt; generated scenery is not transferable player inventory. Direct Vault, tokens and player XP remain zero, with no new monetization or virtual-stock withdrawal.
Current EconomyShopGUI SELL remains current and the planned SELL-off/contracts transition remains future. Neither scenario changes those flows; no sale or contract income is added here.

No rates, work durations, quantities, seed costs, caps, loot, Lands authority, XP or recipes change. Physical-town native loot and SELL unit quotes are unchanged; faster travel can restore realized item income, which is unmeasured and not assumed to be zero. The selected calculator scenario covers Auto-only abstract stock and does not model physical resale. The distinction between current SELL and the future SELL-off/contracts plan is retained.
